title: Grading lab videos
summary: The speaking rubric, the rules that cap a row, missing labs, how to word feedback, and what goes to the coordinator.

la: Grade lab videos with the rubric
Give 0 for every lab not turned in by 5:00 PM
Mark Lab 0 Complete or Not yet

nodes.text: Turned in by the due time?
Face and audio for most of it?
Score the 4 rows, apply the caps

sections.title: Missing labs
steps: Lab not turned in by the due time (5:00 PM): give 0. Every time, even if the student emailed the Lab.
Don't search the inbox, ask why, or wait for a reason.
sections.note: The Lab accepts no late labs. When the coordinator reopens a lab for an Excused Absence, the coordinator grades it and replaces your 0, so you never need to know who or why.

sections.title: Nothing to rate
sections.text: Nothing to rate (0 in every row): no face or no audio for most of the video, mostly not Spanish, a different lab's task, an edited upload, or a video sent outside Bongo. Bongo needs this column to record a 0.

sections.title: Caps
list: **Notecard:** students hold it up to the camera for about 5 seconds at the start. Sentences on the card or the slides: Fluency & Discourse is scored no higher than Does not meet. Rehearsed speech is fine; reading is scored as delivery, not as a separate penalty.
**Slides not visible** in a slide lab for most of the video (Bongo tab or wrong window shared): Task Completion is scored no higher than Does not meet (2). The speaking rows are scored as usual.
**Labs with a video comment:** a missing comment counts as one missing part in Task Completion.
**Lab 0's Bongo setup check** has no rubric: Complete or Not yet, worth 0% of the grade.

sections.title: Feedback
list: Start with what worked, then one thing to improve.
Describe what you hear, not what you suspect: "Try answering with fewer long pauses," not "You were reading."
Use **Record Audio** in the feedback box to model a sound.

sections.title: Honesty concern
steps: Don't mention it in the feedback.
Note the time stamps, the link and the section.
Fill in the Academic Misconduct Form on the Lab Assistant Training SharePoint site.
sections.note: The coordinator decides what happens. You never accuse a student.

sections.title: Coordinator
list: Grade reopened labs with that lab's batch, replacing the 0
Answer grade questions (they come by email)

rows.name: Fluency & Discourse
d: Connected sentences joined with linking words; talks to the camera; pauses only to think.
Mostly complete sentences with some linking words; pauses or restarts don't break the message.
A mix of sentences and fragments with long pauses, or flat, list-like delivery with eyes off the camera.
Mostly single words or fragments with long silences, or recited for most of the video.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rows.name: Comprehensibility & Accuracy
d: Easy to understand throughout; this lab's grammar used correctly.
Understood without effort; this lab's grammar used with a few errors.
Needs a patient listener, or this lab's grammar is missing or often wrong.
Hard to understand even after replaying.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rows.name: Vocabulary Range
d: Varied: chapter words plus descriptive words and different verbs; rarely repeats; no English.
Chapter vocabulary used correctly, with some variety and description.
A small set of words repeated; little description; some English.
Very few words; frequent English or invented words.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).

rows.name: Task Completion
d: Every part answered with specific details; meets the length.
Every part answered; some answers brief; meets the length.
One part missing, or under the length.
Two or more parts missing, or under half the length.
The whole video can't be scored (see below).
